market.headline: Tech led a broad bounce in a short post-Thanksgiving session (QQQ +2.7%, SPY +1.6%), but the S&P 500 is still in a correction, both indexes closed below their 50-day averages, and the market regime is still red and hostile.
market.day_type: Relief bounce on thin holiday volume. The 10-year yield has eased to 4.91 from 5.1, Beijing promised support for its market, and the hardest-hit chip stocks bounced most, but volume was 0.5 of the 20-day average on QQQ and 0.6 on SPY, so the bounce shows little real conviction.
watch: QQQ 663.51 and SPY 730.98: a close above both means the bounce is real. A drop under today's lows (636.72 and 719.62) means the selloff is back.
Mon Dec 1: JOLTS job openings at 10:00, then MRVL, MDB and NTAP earnings (dates estimated). MRVL is the first chip test since NVDA's shipment pause.
Wed Dec 2: CRM and SNOW earnings (estimated), the software check for ORCL. Fri Dec 4: payrolls at 08:30.

stocks.headline: Up only 0.8% to 150.49 while QQQ rose 2.7%. It is still 38.2% below its high. Morning call: right (it lagged).
stocks.why: The business is not the problem: sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and next year's profit forecasts rose 28% in 90 days. The stock is held down by two things the numbers don't capture. First, the CEO scandal and his return raise governance questions. Second, Nvidia has told partners to pause server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries as the US tightens chip exports to China. The pause hits sales in that region and spreads to its suppliers and server builders (MU, TSM, SMCI). That is why NVDA lagged on a day when the rest of the chip group bounced hard.

long_term.reason: At 9 times next year's forecast profit, the stock prices in a lot of bad news. But the export pause and the governance questions are still open, so this is not yet a buy, which agrees with the house Hold.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the pause is lifted quickly and the board fixes governance, this moves to Add on dips. If the spy claims gain any support or the export ban widens, it moves to Trim.
stocks.action: Don't buy Monday. Add only near 124.5, or after a close back above 169.32.

levels.means: above = the 52-week low holds and this is the add zone; below = the scandal is being priced as lasting damage
above = today's bounce holds; below = it gave up the whole holiday bounce, so expect a retest of 124.5
above = it is back over its 20-day average and buyers have returned; below = the downtrend is intact

stocks.headline: Up 7.6% to 646.95, the best gain on the list, but still down 30.8% over 20 days. Morning call: wrong for the day (it ran well past 615.26).
stocks.why: MU moves about twice as much as the market, so a tech bounce lifts it hardest. It also got a boost from the record jump in Chinese chip stocks. The business is booming: sales are up 345%, the operating margin is 75%, there is $134.0B in contracted backlog, and it trades at 2.9 times next year's forecast profit. The stock is cheap because the market doubts AI spending will last, and NVDA's Southeast Asia pause directly threatens demand for MU's memory. The Dec 17 report (estimated), with a typical move of 8%, will decide whether the market believes the profit forecasts.

long_term.reason: The results are among the strongest on the list, but the stock is below all its main averages on light volume. Buying before a report known for 8% swings is a bet, not an investment, so this agrees with the house Wait.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A strong Dec 17 report with a solid outlook while the price holds 607.27 makes it a Buy.
stocks.action: No new money before the Dec 17 report. Holders keep their shares, and a close under 607.27 means today's bounce has failed.

levels.means: above = the bounce holds; below = it erased today's gain and is heading back to 548.13
above = it broke today's high and the bounce has follow-through; below = it is stalling
above = it reclaimed the 20-day average and the trend is turning; below = the bounce is still inside a downtrend

stocks.headline: Up 3.1% to 107.13. It held above 105.84 and filled the first half-position. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: The stock is down 56.9% from its high because the market is punishing anyone tied to AI data-center spending. The business is moving the other way: sales growth sped up to 30%, contracted backlog is $664.0B, and it trades at 9.4 times next year's forecast profit, its cheapest P/E in 5 years. The risk is the Dec 14 report (estimated), where analysts expect profit per share to fall 16% from a year ago and the stock usually moves 11%. The backlog only turns into profit if the build-out keeps getting funded. CRM and SNOW report on Dec 2 and set the tone for software stocks before then.

long_term.reason: Accelerating sales and a huge backlog at a five-year-low P/E make this the best value on the list, which agrees with the house Buy now.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A Dec 14 report with backlog shrinking or no outlook, or a close below the 99.34 low, moves this back to Wait.
stocks.action: Keep the first half. Don't add before Dec 14, and buy the second half after the report if it stays above 105.84.

levels.means: above = the 52-week low holds and the thesis stands; below = stop adding, because the market is pricing real damage
above = it reclaimed the 20-day average and the turn is confirmed; below = it is still basing
